mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive monthly releases
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between GDPC1 < -2% and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase above 0.4 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate hiring, which in turn depresses earnings and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower (p > 0.10) following UNRATE increases > 0.4pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between three-month INDPRO decline > -1.5% and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decrease in both FEDFUNDS and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.25 percentage points indicates aggressive monetary easing alongside falling inflation, which boosts risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls > -0.25pp AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.25% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL decline > -0.25% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1.5% signals a strengthening consumer demand environment, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation (p > 0.05) between RSAFS > 1.5% and subsequent 20-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE in the same month indicates robust labor market expansion, which increases consumer purchasing power and corporate hiring, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when both PAYEMS and UNRATE rise in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below 900,000 units for four consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which reduces construction sector earnings and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between four-month HOUST < 900k streak and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.
